{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Read the data
sales = pd.read_csv('data/sales.csv')

# Clean revenue: remove commas and convert to float
sales['revenue_clean'] = sales['revenue'].str.replace(',', '').astype(float)

# Identify QA orders
qa_mask = sales['revenue_clean'] == 999999.99

# Filter out QA orders and refunded orders
# Population: all orders excluding refunded orders and QA orders
filtered_data = sales[~qa_mask & (sales['status'] == 'completed')]

# Verify the population
print(f'Number of rows in filtered_data: {len(filtered_data)}')
print(f'Number of QA orders excluded: {qa_mask.sum()}')
print(f'Number of refunded orders excluded: {sales[sales["status"] == "refunded"].shape[0]}')

# Compute conversion rate by customer_segment
conversion_rates = (
    filtered_data
    .groupby('customer_segment')['converted']
    .agg(['count', 'sum'])
    .rename(columns={'count': 'total_completed', 'sum': 'converted_count'})
)

# Compute conversion rate as percentage
conversion_rates['conversion_rate_percent'] = (conversion_rates['converted_count'] / conversion_rates['total_completed']) * 100

# Sort by conversion rate descending
conversion_rates_sorted = conversion_rates.sort_values(by='conversion_rate_percent', ascending=False)

# Output the results
print(conversion_rates_sorted)

# Get the segment with highest rate
highest_segment = conversion_rates_sorted.index[0]
print(f'Highest conversion rate segment: {highest_segment}')"}
